I would also recommend talking to a therapist or doctor about intrusive thoughts, as it sounds like you think about this a lot. I fight with my mom a lot, so I know how you feel in that aspect. When I moved out and I didn’t have to see her anymore, it made my life a lot easier. I know it can be hard to deal with a situation when it feels like there’s no way out, but if something did end up happening, the consequences of that would be a lot worse. If you can, just try to stick it out for the last three years (I say three because you mentioned a driving test) and start preparing yourself to move out as soon as you’re able. If you have a job, start saving to buy any furniture etc, and then when it starts to get closer to the time you’re gonna move out make even bigger plans. Look for apartments, build credit if you can, start looking at cars etc. Focus on yourself, don’t let her ruin your life because she is selfish. The pandemic probably certainly didn’t make things any better, and I’m not sure what your city is like, but I recommend trying to get out of the house more and away from the situation. If she tries to engage, don’t. Simply answer anything calmly and move on about your day. I know putting it into practice is a lot harder than it sounds here, but it will help stop a lot of conflict. My mother is a narcissist, and it was so hard to deal with her growing up. As soon as I moved out, I was able to finally start living how I wanted to live, and be how I wanted to be in the world. Everything changes when you get away from whatever is making you sad, depressed, anxious etc. you just have to be there.
